lesson_title: Same Birthday, Same City, Different Chances
hook_text: Two girls, born on the same day in the same city. Why do they start life so far apart?
clip_script: Lindiwe and Megan share a birthday, love netball and want to be doctors. Lindiwe lives far from town, where her grandparents were moved under apartheid. Her dad lost his job. Fifty learners in her class, no lab, one textbook for two. Megan lives near town in her grandparents' house. Thirty in her class, a lab and a maths tutor. Neither chose this. History shaped it: land taken, the Land Act, Group Areas, Bantu Education. Today unemployment and unequal schools keep the gap wide. That gap in chances is inequality. And it is exactly what education, skills and jobs can start to close.
visual_style: A whiteboard split screen of two girls' days side by side, with a timeline of laws underneath and a gap arrow between them.
mood: Serious and fair, honest without being hopeless.
pacing: Parallel scenes cutting between the two girls, then a calm explanation of causes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and list three things that could narrow the gap between Lindiwe and Megan.
